name: TPS3702CX33DDCR
title: TPS3702: high-accuracy overvoltage and undervoltage window detector in SOT-23-THIN
summary: A window voltage detector that watches one SENSE input against a fixed undervoltage and a fixed overvoltage threshold, both set inside the part with no external divider, and flags each fault on its own active-low open-drain output. Threshold accuracy is ±0.25% typical and ±0.9% from –40 °C to 125 °C; a SET pin picks one of two built-in threshold pairs. It runs from 2 V to 18 V on its own VDD pin at 7 µA typical. TPS3702CX33DDCR is the 3.3 V version with ±4% (SET high) or ±9% (SET low) nominal thresholds and 0.55% hysteresis, on a 3000-piece reel.

pins.name: UV
pins.function: Undervoltage flag, active low. Pulls low once SENSE drops under the falling threshold VIT–(UV); needs a pull-up resistor to the logic level wanted.

pins.name: SENSE
pins.function: The voltage being watched. Below the undervoltage threshold UV goes low; above the overvoltage threshold OV goes low.

pins.name: SET
pins.function: Selects which of the two built-in threshold pairs is used: high for the tighter window, low for the wider one.

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Device supply, 2 V to 18 V. A 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor placed near the pin is recommended.

pins.name: OV
pins.function: Overvoltage flag, active low. Pulls low once SENSE climbs over the rising threshold VIT+(OV); needs a pull-up resistor to the logic level wanted.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: One rail of up to 5 V feeds SENSE directly and also powers a processor. The detector's own VDD may come from a separate supply of up to 18 V, and SET is driven from a level of up to 6.5 V to choose the band. Each open-drain output has its own pull-up to the monitored rail: UV drives the processor's reset input, OV its non-maskable interrupt.

parts.value: Nominal monitored rail, up to 5 V

circuits.title: Figure 7-2. Window voltage detector schematic
circuits.description: The basic window detector: the device runs from a 2 V to 18 V supply and watches a separate input of up to 6.5 V on SENSE. SET is grounded, which picks the wider band. UV and OV are tied into one wired-OR line with a single pull-up to the supply; that line goes low on either fault and feeds a system reset or enable input.

circuits.title: Figure 7-6. ±5% window voltage detector for SOC power rails
circuits.description: Three detectors guard the 3.3 V, 1.8 V and 1.2 V rails of an SOC. All three run from 3.3 V. Each one's SENSE and SET are tied to the rail it watches, so SET is high and the ±4% nominal band applies. Every UV and OV pin joins a single line with one pull-up to 3.3 V per detector, and that line drives the SOC's RESET input.

where.VIT: the threshold in question: VIT– for UV, VIT+ for OV

equations.note: A smaller overdrive gives a slower output response.

operation.text: Inside are two comparators, a precision reference and a trimmed divider, so one SENSE input is checked against an undervoltage and an overvoltage limit with no external resistors; the divider's tolerance is already inside the accuracy figures. Each output goes low when SENSE leaves the window. Each output tolerates a pull-up of up to 18 V and sinks as much as 10 mA.

SENSE may sit anywhere from 0 V to 6.5 V (7.0 V absolute maximum) regardless of VDD. Both comparators have built-in hysteresis. UV goes low when SENSE falls under VIT–(UV) and releases to high impedance once SENSE climbs back over VIT–(UV) + VHYS; OV goes low when SENSE rises over VIT+(OV) and releases once SENSE falls under VIT+(OV) – VHYS. In noisy systems a 1 nF to 10 nF capacitor on SENSE lowers sensitivity to transients, though it is usually not needed.

The two fault-entry thresholds, VIT–(UV) on a falling SENSE and VIT+(OV) on a rising SENSE, are the ones held to the stated accuracy. Coming back into the window from outside, the levels are offset by the hysteresis.

UV and OV are open-drain and need pull-up resistors, which may go to any rail up to 18 V independent of VDD, so the flags can match the logic level of whatever they drive: a processor's reset or enable, or the enable of a regulator. The pull-up value is set by VOL, the capacitive load and the leakage ID(leak). Tying UV and OV together gives one wired-OR line that goes low on either fault.

Every device carries two threshold pairs. SET above VIH(SET) selects the tighter window, below VIL(SET) the wider one. For a TPS3702Cxxx the nominal thresholds are ±4% with SET high and ±9% with SET low; adding the ±0.9% threshold accuracy, the worst-case band is ±4.9% or ±9.9%. Switching SET lets a system tolerate a wider band during start-up and tighten it once running. SET has an internal pull-up current of 600 nA typical.
Once VDD has been above UVLO for about 300 µs (tSD), the outputs follow SENSE as in the truth table.
With VDD between V(POR) and UVLO, UV is held low and OV is high impedance whatever SENSE does. UVLO on a falling VDD lies between 1.3 V and 1.7 V.
Below V(POR), 0.8 V maximum, the device cannot hold an output low and both output states are undefined.

An external resistor divider lets SENSE watch a rail above its range or one with no matching nominal option. The SENSE input current flows only through the top resistor and adds error, so the divider current should be more than about 100 times ISENSE; TI application report SLVA450 covers divider design.

Pick the version whose nominal voltage and band fit the rail from the naming convention table; a divider can scale a rail that has no matching option. The output rise time after release is set by the pull-up and the node capacitance; choose the pull-up for both the timing downstream and a low enough VOL at the sink current. For light capacitive loads, 10 kΩ to 1 MΩ suits.
Short spikes on SENSE do not trip the outputs. Whether a transient trips depends on both how long it lasts and its overdrive.

VDD runs from 2 V to 18 V. No input capacitor is required; with a noisy supply a 0.1 µF capacitor from VDD to GND is good practice. VDD is rated 20 V absolute maximum, so a supply that may see transients above 20 V needs extra protection.

Keep the VDD bypass capacitor next to the part and its supply trace short; trace inductance in series with that capacitor makes a resonant circuit whose ringing can overshoot the VDD maximum. The example layout places the two output pull-ups beside pins 1 and 6 and the VDD capacitor beside pin 5.
An automotive version, TPS3702-Q1, is qualified to AEC-Q100. The TPS3702CX33EVM-683 evaluation module carries this device.
